    if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$D/badexe-out" "$badexe" 2>/dev/null; then
      bad "a wrapper path containing '$badexe' is refused" "    exited 0"
    else
      ok "a wrapper path containing shell/sed metacharacters is refused ($badexe)"
    fi
    rm -f "$D/badexe-out"
  done

  # A directory passes `-r`, so without the `-f` test this would fall through to sed
  # and abort activation instead of taking the quiet no-Steam branch.
  mkdir -p "$D/srcdir"
  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/srcdir" "$D/srcdir-out" "$W" 2>/dev/null; then
    if [ ! -e "$D/srcdir-out" ]; then ok "a directory as source is the quiet no-op, not an error"
    else bad "a directory as source is the quiet no-op, not an error" "    wrote a file"; fi
  else
    bad "a directory as source is the quiet no-op, not an error" "    exited non-zero"
  fi

  mkdir -p "$D/dstdir"
  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$D/dstdir" "$W" 2>/dev/null; then
    bad "a directory as destination is refused" "    exited 0; mv would have hidden a file inside it"
  else
    ok "a directory as destination is refused"
  fi

  echo
  echo "--- the no-Steam branch cleans up after itself ------------------------------"

  # If Steam leaves system/packages.shiori, the source stops being readable and this
  # branch runs forever. Leaving the override behind is the worst shape available:
  # ~/.local/share outranks /usr/share, so a dead Exec= keeps shadowing the packaged
  # entry, and after GC the launcher entry still looks right and silently does nothing.
  printf '[Desktop Entry]\nName=Steam\nExec=/nix/store/oldhash-steam/bin/steam %%U\n' > "$D/stale"
  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/absent.desktop" "$D/stale" "$W" 2>/dev/null; then
    if [ ! -e "$D/stale" ]; then ok "a stale override we wrote is removed when Steam goes away"
    else bad "a stale override we wrote is removed when Steam goes away" "    still present"; fi
  else
    bad "a stale override we wrote is removed when Steam goes away" "    exited non-zero"
  fi

  # ...but only one of ours. A hand-written steam.desktop is not ours to delete.
  printf '[Desktop Entry]\nName=Steam\nExec=/usr/bin/steam %%U\n' > "$D/handmade"
  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/absent.desktop" "$D/handmade" "$W" 2>/dev/null; then
    if [ -e "$D/handmade" ]; then ok "a hand-written steam.desktop is left alone"
    else bad "a hand-written steam.desktop is left alone" "    deleted a file we did not write"; fi
  else
    bad "a hand-written steam.desktop is left alone" "    exited non-zero"
  fi

  rm -f "$D/never"
  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/absent.desktop" "$D/never" "$W" 2>"$D/err3"; then
    if [ ! -e "$D/never" ] && [ ! -s "$D/err3" ]; then
      ok "an absent source with nothing to clean exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing"
    else
      bad "an absent source with nothing to clean exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing" \
        "    created: $([ -e "$D/never" ] && echo yes || echo no), stderr: $(cat "$D/err3")"
    fi
  else
    bad "an absent source with nothing to clean exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing" "    exited non-zero"
  fi

  echo
  echo "--- re-running, which is what every hms after the first does ----------------"

  # The exit status is checked, not discarded: this is the only case covering
  # "destination already exists", and if the second run failed outright the file
  # would still be byte-identical and a content-only assertion would report ok.
  before=$(cat "$out")
  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" "$W" 2>"$D/err4"; then
    if [ "$before" = "$(cat "$out")" ]; then ok "re-running over an existing override is idempotent"
    else bad "re-running over an existing override is idempotent" "    second run changed the file"; fi
  else
    bad "re-running over an existing override is idempotent" "$(sed 's/^/      /' "$D/err4")"
  fi

  # A SIGKILL mid-switch skips the EXIT trap; nothing else ever sweeps the residue,
  # and a leftover is invisible to XDG scanners but permanent.
  touch "$(dirname "$out")/steam.desktop.ABCDEF"
  bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" "$W" 2>/dev/null
  leftovers=$(find "$(dirname "$out")" -name 'steam.desktop.??????' | wc -l)
  if [ "$leftovers" = 0 ]; then ok "a leftover temp from a killed run is swept"
  else bad "a leftover temp from a killed run is swept" "    found $leftovers"; fi
fi

echo
[ "$skips" -gt 0 ] && echo "$skips of $n cases skipped"
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "all $n cases passed"
else
  echo "$fails of $n cases FAILED"
fi
exit $((fails > 0))

input.new_string:
The `steam` wrapper (in `home.nix`) and `home/steam-desktop-override` model the two
places nix's profile and a pacman-installed app collide. Steam shells out to
`xdg-user-dir`, `~/.nix-profile/bin` precedes `/usr/bin`, and nix's loader can't
satisfy what Arch's `libc.so.6` leaves undefined — `__pointer_chk_guard`; and
`GIO_EXTRA_MODULES` points Steam's sniper runtime at a gvfs module its older glib
can't load. The wrapper prepends the host's directories rather than sanitising nix
away, because `xdg-open` exists *only* in the profile here and is how Steam opens a
link, so the cases assert both directions — a fix that satisfies one and breaks the
other looks correct from either side alone. Three of them are there because the
obvious assertion passes with the bug still in place: the `xdg-user-dir` case reads
through `readlink` (profile entries are symlinks, so the unresolved name is never a
store path), the `xdg-open` case *executes* it rather than resolving it (a `command
-v` check can only fail when the case above it already has), and a first case
asserts the `/usr/bin`-vs-profile collision still exists at all, without which the
rest can pass having measured nothing. The `nix eval` cases cover the wiring, since
the wrapper and the script can both be correct while the activation entry passes the
wrong paths — including that the entry keeps its `|| warnEcho`, because activation
runs under `set -eu` and a bare failure here would abort the entries after it.

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q --amend -F - <<'MSG'
home: launch Steam through a wrapper that prefers the host's helpers

Steam is the pacman package, but it inherits a PATH whose first entry is
~/.nix-profile/bin, and that breaks it in one measured way. Steam shells out to
`xdg-user-dir <key>` (the string in steamclient.so is the format `xdg-user-dir
%s`) to locate a user directory; xdg.userDirs.enable puts nix's xdg-user-dirs in
the profile, so the call lands on the nix copy. Measured on shiori 2026-09-28,
once per launch:

  xdg-user-dir: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/libc.so.6: undefined symbol:
  __pointer_chk_guard, version GLIBC_PRIVATE

The mechanism runs the opposite way to what the message suggests, and the first
draft of this commit had it backwards. Measured with `nm -D`: Arch's ld.so
*defines* __pointer_chk_guard@@GLIBC_PRIVATE and Arch's libc.so.6 leaves it
*undefined*, expecting its own loader to supply it; nix's glibc 2.42 defines it in
neither. The nix binary keeps nix's hardcoded ELF interpreter, Steam's runtime puts
Arch's /usr/lib/libc.so.6 in its library path, and nix's older loader cannot
satisfy that newer libc's reference -- which is why the error names
/usr/lib/libc.so.6 as the referrer rather than the binary.

The fix prepends the host's directories rather than sanitising nix out of PATH, and
the difference is load-bearing: `xdg-open` exists ONLY in the profile here, because
Arch's xdg-utils is not installed, and it is how Steam opens a link. That it *works*
from there is a second fact worth recording, because nix's xdg-open dies identically
under a Steam-runtime library path: steam.sh saves this wrapper's environment as
SYSTEM_PATH/SYSTEM_LD_LIBRARY_PATH (:135) and restores it before handing a URL to an
external handler (:1015), so the handler gets a clean library path where the
in-process xdg-user-dir call did not.

The cost, stated because it is larger than the fix: this reorders name resolution
for Steam's whole descendant tree, not just Steam -- games, Proton helpers, anything
a launch option invokes, and via SYSTEM_PATH the external handlers too. Nothing is
removed, and the reordering runs toward root-owned directories (/usr/local/bin and
/usr/bin are root:root here; ~/.nix-profile/bin is under $HOME). A shim directory
holding only xdg-user-dir would scope it tighter; prepending is preferred because it
needs no list of which helpers to redirect, and that list is what would rot.

GIO_EXTRA_MODULES (env.nix) is unset for a related reason: steamwebhelper logged
`libgvfscommon.so: undefined symbol: g_task_set_static_name` twice per launch. Only
the *sniper runtime's* glib is too old -- Arch's glib2 is 2.88.3, the same version
nix's gvfs is built against, and it exports the symbol, so the host is not part of
this and an earlier draft claiming otherwise was wrong. Steam's UI is CEF, not GTK,
so the volume monitor that variable exists for buys Steam nothing. Unset by name,
not by a GIO_* sweep, so GIO_MODULE_DIR survives.

Env, not argv, is what the wrapper changes -- which is what makes it survive the
launch paths STEAM_FORCE_DESKTOPUI_SCALING was chosen for in 10fabaf. The tray's
"restart Steam" re-execs /usr/bin/steam and bypasses the wrapper *script*, but an
exec inherits the environment, so both fixes hold where a -flag would not.

home/steam-desktop-override is the other half: elephant/walker and xdg-open exec the
desktop file's Exec= line, not $PATH. It rewrites the pacman file at activation
instead of mirroring it -- steam.desktop is 282 lines, a Comment= plus 26
translations then nine Desktop Actions with their own, and only the ten Exec= need
to differ.

Its failure policy is the part that took the most getting right. The generated
`activate` runs under `set -eu` (verified: line 2 of a built generation), and this
entry sorts after linkGeneration and reloadSystemd but BEFORE zenInstallsIni. A bare
non-zero exit would therefore not merely skip the launcher fix: it would abort the
rest of activation, leaving the profile already pointing at the new generation while
gcroots/current-home still names the old one, and leaving installs.ini for Zen to
re-pin. So the call site appends `|| warnEcho` and degrades to "Steam launches
unwrapped" -- the same call system/deploy already makes with `./thermald-setup ||
echo ... continuing`.

Three silent failures the first draft had, each now loud:
  - A source whose Exec= shape changed matched nothing, and a verbatim copy got
    installed at a path that OUTRANKS /usr/share -- the original bug, behind a file
    that looks like the fix. Now refused via a post-condition.
  - The no-Steam branch left a stale override forever. Once its store path is
    garbage-collected the launcher entry still looks right and does nothing. Now
    removed, matched on its rewritten Exec= so a hand-written file is left alone.
  - A directory as source passed `-r` and fell through to sed; a directory as
    destination made mv hide the file inside it and exit 0. Both refused.

tests/steam-env.sh drives both halves plus the home.nix wiring through 39 cases,
and every guard was checked against a mutation that should break it. Fifteen
mutations run: five on the wrapper (dropping the PATH prepend restores the original
error, dropping the GIO unset, sanitising nix out entirely, unquoting "$@", widening
the unset to GIO_MODULE_DIR), nine on the rewrite, and one on home.nix removing
`|| warnEcho`. Two mutations changed nothing and both were real findings rather than
weak tests: a separate emptiness check was dead code (the post-condition already
refuses an empty source) and is gone, and of the three metacharacter cases only
whitespace needs the up-front validation, which the comment now says.

Three cases exist because the obvious assertion passes with the bug still in place:
the xdg-user-dir case reads through readlink (profile entries are symlinks, so the
unresolved name is never a store path), the xdg-open case executes it rather than
resolving it (a `command -v` check can only fail when the case above it already
has), and a first case asserts the collision still exists at all.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copy a packaged steam.desktop, rewriting every Exec=/usr/bin/steam to a wrapper.
#
#   steam-desktop-override <src> <dst> <wrapper>
#
# Called from home.nix's steamDesktopOverride activation entry, which passes
# /usr/share/applications/steam.desktop, ~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop
# and the `steam` wrapper it builds. See the wrapper's comment in home.nix for why
# Steam needs to be launched through one at all.
#
# A script here, rather than the whole file mirrored into home.nix the way
# Zoom.desktop is: steam.desktop is 282 lines -- a Comment= plus 26 translations of
# it, then nine Desktop Actions, eight of which carry 26 translations of their own
# Name= (BigPicture has none) -- and the only lines that need to differ are the ten
# Exec=. Deriving the file from the pacman one also means a steam.desktop changed by
# a package update is picked up by the next `hms` instead of silently drifting from a
# copy in this repo.
#
# Do NOT also declare this path via xdg.dataFile: home-manager's linkGeneration
# would link a store symlink at the same name this script mv's over, and the two
# would fight, with hm's next-generation cleanup operating on a file it no longer
# recognises. The adjacent Zoom.desktop block in home.nix is exactly that pattern,
# which is what makes the mistake inviting.
#
# EXIT STATUS IS ADVISORY, and the call site treats it that way. Every failure path
# below is non-zero and loud, but home.nix appends `|| warnEcho`, because a
# home-manager activation script runs under `set -eu`: a bare non-zero here would
# abort every later activation entry, leaving the new generation already current
# while gcroots/current-home still names the old one. Degrading to "Steam launches
# unwrapped" beats that, which is the same call system/deploy makes when it runs
# ./thermald-setup with `|| echo ... continuing`.
set -eu

src=${1:?source desktop file}
dst=${2:?destination desktop file}
exe=${3:?wrapper to point Exec= at}

# The line that makes an override recognisable as ours. Matched literally when
# deciding whether a leftover file is one we may delete, so it must NOT be derived
# from the wrapper's store path: keying the check on `-steam` in the path meant that
# renaming the derivation silently stopped the cleanup below from ever matching. A
# `#` line is a comment per the Desktop Entry spec and is ignored by launchers.
marker='# generated by dotfiles home/steam-desktop-override -- do not edit'

# $exe lands in both a sed replacement and a Desktop Entry Exec= field, and the
# metacharacters of those two grammars do not overlap. Rather than escape for each,
# refuse anything outside the character set a nix store path can hold -- which
# includes `?` and `=`, so they are in the class even though no name here uses them.
#
# What this actually buys, measured rather than assumed: WHITESPACE is the only case
# nothing else catches -- a space would split the Exec= field and silently launch the
# wrong thing. Were this guard removed, `|` would make sed die and `&` would reinsert
# the match, which the post-condition further down then refuses; both stay caught,
# just with a worse error. It is here for the space, and for saying so legibly.
case $exe in
  *[!A-Za-z0-9/._+=?-]*)
    echo "$0: refusing a wrapper path with shell/sed-significant characters: $exe" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# A source that is not there at all means this host has no Steam -- so if a previous
# generation left an override behind, it is now stale and must go. Leaving it is the
# worst shape available: ~/.local/share outranks /usr/share, so the dead file keeps
# shadowing the packaged entry, and once the store path in its Exec= is
# garbage-collected the launcher entry still looks right and silently does nothing.
#
# Only a file carrying our marker is removed, so a hand-written steam.desktop is left
# alone. The removal says so on stderr: it is the one state change here that is not a
# failure, and a silent delete of a working launcher entry is not something to do
# without a word.
if [ ! -e "$src" ]; then
  if [ -f "$dst" ] && grep -qxF "$marker" "$dst"; then
    rm -f "$dst"
    echo "$0: no $src; removed the override this script had written at $dst" >&2
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Present but not a readable regular file is an anomaly, NOT "this host has no
# Steam" -- a directory there, or a mode that hides it, should not be able to delete
# a working override or be mistaken for the quiet path above.
if ! { [ -f "$src" ] && [ -r "$src" ]; }; then
  echo "$0: $src exists but is not a readable regular file" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# mv is rename(2), which replaces the destination NAME -- so a stale home-manager
# symlink at $dst is replaced rather than written through into the read-only store.
# A directory there is the one case rename cannot handle the way we want (POSIX mv
# would move the temp file *inside* it and exit 0, a silent no-op), so rule it out.
if [ -d "$dst" ]; then
  echo "$0: $dst is a directory, refusing to write an override there" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"

# Sweep temps a SIGKILL left behind (an OOM kill mid-switch skips the EXIT trap).
# The `hm-` infix is what keeps this glob off real files: a bare `.??????` also
# matches steam.desktop.backup, which is someone's deliberate copy.
rm -f "$dst".hm-??????

tmp=$(mktemp "$dst.hm-XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

# Two anchored patterns rather than one with \b, which is a GNU sed extension:
# activation runs on Darwin too, and while the gate above means sed is never reached
# there today, a pattern that only works under GNU sed is a trap for whoever moves
# this next. Anchoring also does the job \b was for -- neither matches a hypothetical
# Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo, nor a key that merely ends in the same path such as
# X-Not-Exec=.
{
  printf '%s\n' "$marker"
  sed -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam |Exec=$exe |" \
      -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam\$|Exec=$exe|" \
      "$src"
} > "$tmp"

# The post-condition, and the point of the whole exercise. Deriving the file from the
# pacman copy was chosen so a package update is picked up rather than drifting
# silently -- but a FAILED derivation is exactly as silent as the drift it replaced.
#
# Both halves are needed, and the second is the one that matters in practice. "At
# least one line was rewritten" would pass a PARTIAL rewrite: the real file has ten
# Exec= lines, one main and nine Desktop Actions, and an update that changed only the

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q --amend -F - <<'MSG'
home: launch Steam through a wrapper that prefers the host's helpers

Steam is the pacman package, but it inherits a PATH whose first entry is
~/.nix-profile/bin, and that breaks it in one measured way. Steam shells out to
`xdg-user-dir <key>` (the string in steamclient.so is the format `xdg-user-dir %s`)
to locate a user directory; xdg.userDirs.enable puts nix's xdg-user-dirs in the
profile, so the call lands on the nix copy. Measured on shiori 2026-09-28, once per
launch:

  xdg-user-dir: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/libc.so.6: undefined symbol:
  __pointer_chk_guard, version GLIBC_PRIVATE

The mechanism is a mismatched loader/libc pair, and it runs the opposite way to what
the message suggests at a glance. Measured with `nm -D`: Arch's ld.so *defines*
__pointer_chk_guard@@GLIBC_PRIVATE and Arch's libc.so.6 (2.44) leaves it *undefined*,
expecting its own loader to supply it; nix's glibc 2.42 defines it in neither. The nix
binary keeps nix's hardcoded ELF interpreter, Steam's runtime puts Arch's
/usr/lib/libc.so.6 in its library path, and nix's older loader cannot satisfy that
newer libc's reference -- which is why the error names /usr/lib/libc.so.6 as the
referrer rather than the binary.

The fix prepends the host's directories rather than sanitising nix out of PATH, and
the difference is load-bearing: `xdg-open` exists ONLY in the profile here, because
Arch's xdg-utils is not installed, and it is how Steam opens a link. That it *works*
from there is a second fact worth recording, because nix's xdg-open dies identically
under a Steam-runtime library path. steam.sh saves this wrapper's environment as
SYSTEM_PATH/SYSTEM_LD_LIBRARY_PATH (:135-136) and steamclient.so, which references
both names, restores them for an external handler. Not steam.sh:1015 -- that restore
is on the restart path, feeding the MAGIC_RESTART_EXITCODE re-exec, and an earlier
draft of this commit miscited it. It does mean the tray's restart re-execs
/usr/bin/steam with SYSTEM_PATH, i.e. this wrapper's already-prepended PATH, so the
fix survives that too.

The cost, stated because it is larger than the fix: this reorders name resolution for
Steam's whole descendant tree, not just Steam -- games, Proton helpers, anything a
launch option invokes, and via SYSTEM_PATH the external handlers too. Nothing is
removed, and the reordering runs toward root-owned directories (/usr/local/bin and
/usr/bin are root:root here; ~/.nix-profile/bin is under $HOME). A shim directory
holding only xdg-user-dir would scope it tighter; prepending is preferred because it
needs no list of which helpers to redirect, and that list is what would rot.

GIO_EXTRA_MODULES (env.nix) is unset for a related reason: steamwebhelper logged
`libgvfscommon.so: undefined symbol: g_task_set_static_name` twice per launch. The
host is not part of this -- Arch's glib2 is 2.88.3, the same version nix's gvfs is
built against, and it exports the symbol. g_task_set_static_name landed in glib 2.76,
while the runtime that logged it (steamrt64/pv-runtime, steamrt3c, which is what the
journal names) ships 2.66.8 and the scout runtime the 32-bit client runs under ships
2.58.3. An earlier draft blamed "sniper"; this install has none, steam.sh rm -fr's it
as "now replaced by steamrt3c". Steam's UI is CEF, not GTK, so the volume monitor
that variable exists for buys Steam nothing. Unset by name, not by a GIO_* sweep.

home/steam-desktop-override is the other half: elephant/walker and xdg-open exec the
desktop file's Exec= line, not $PATH. It rewrites the pacman file at activation
instead of mirroring it -- steam.desktop is 282 lines, a Comment= plus 26 translations
then nine Desktop Actions (eight with 26 translations of their own Name=) -- and only
the ten Exec= need to differ.

Its failure policy is the part that took the most getting right. The generated
`activate` runs under `set -eu` (verified: line 2 of a built generation), and this
entry sorts after linkGeneration and reloadSystemd but BEFORE zenInstallsIni. A bare
non-zero exit would therefore not merely skip the launcher fix: it would abort the
rest of activation, leaving the profile already pointing at the new generation while
gcroots/current-home still names the old one, and leaving installs.ini for Zen to
re-pin. So the call site appends `|| warnEcho` and degrades to "Steam launches
unwrapped" -- the same call system/deploy makes with `./thermald-setup || echo ...
continuing`.

Five ways this could have failed silently, each now loud:
  - A source whose Exec= shape changed matched nothing, and a verbatim copy got
    installed at a path that OUTRANKS /usr/share -- the original bug, behind a file
    that looks like the fix. Refused by a post-condition.
  - A PARTIAL rewrite passed that post-condition: the real file has ten Exec= lines,
    and an update changing only the nine Desktop Action ones would leave every
    right-click action unwrapped while the main entry satisfied "did anything get
    rewritten?". Now no line that looks like a target may survive -- and the survivor
    class is "the name ends here", not "a space follows", because the first version of
    that check let a tab-separated survivor through. Its own test case caught that.
  - The no-Steam branch left a stale override forever; after GC the launcher entry
    still looks right and does nothing. Now removed -- keyed on a marker line the
    script writes, NOT on guessing `-steam` in the store path, which would have
    stopped matching the moment the wrapper derivation were renamed.
  - "Not a readable regular file" was treated as "this host has no Steam", so a
    directory or a bad mode could delete a working override. Those are now separated:
    genuinely absent is the quiet path, anything else is an error.
  - The temp sweep globbed `.??????`, exactly six characters, and so deleted a user's
    steam.desktop.backup on every hms. The template carries an `hm-` infix now.

tests/steam-env.sh drives both halves plus the home.nix wiring through 42 cases, and
every guard was checked against a mutation that should break it -- 21 in total, and
the mutation log is the reason several of the above exist. Two mutations changed no
case's result, and both were findings rather than weak tests: a separate emptiness
check was dead code (the post-condition already refuses an empty source) and is gone,
and of the three metacharacter cases only whitespace needs the up-front validation,
which the comment now says.

Five cases exist because the obvious assertion passes with the bug still in place:
the xdg-user-dir case reads through readlink (profile entries are symlinks, so the
unresolved name is never a store path); the xdg-open case executes it rather than
resolving it (a `command -v` check can only fail when the case above it already has);
a first case asserts the collision still exists at all; the wiring case compares
argument ORDER, since checking that each path merely appears somewhere passes a
src/dst transposition; and the fixture wrapper path deliberately does not end in
`-steam`, so the marker predicate cannot be satisfied by luck.
